title: False Sharing Elimination
description: Pads independently-updated fields to separate cache lines so cores stop invalidating each other's caches. Two counters in one 64-byte line ping-pong on every increment; padding makes each core's line private. It is the first fix for contended data.

demo.title: Demo — False Sharing Elimination

title: Cache-Line Padding
description: Pads hot structures to whole cache lines with explicit alignment attributes. Padding wastes a little memory to save a lot of coherence traffic. Compilers offer alignas and attributes for exactly this.
key_mechanisms: Pad to multiples of the line size
Keep padding out of serialized forms

demo.title: Demo — Cache-Line Padding

title: NUMA-Local Allocation
description: Allocates memory on the NUMA node where the using threads run. Remote-node access costs 1.5 to 2x local latency; first-touch placement usually gets it right. Pinning threads completes the picture.
key_mechanisms: Allocate with first-touch or explicit policy

demo.title: Demo — NUMA-Local Allocation

title: Software Prefetching
description: Issues software prefetches for data needed a few iterations ahead. Prefetch hides memory latency when the access pattern is predictable; hardware prefetchers handle the simple cases. It helps pointer-chasing and sparse loops.

demo.title: Demo — Software Prefetching

title: Cache Coloring
description: Colors pages so hot data spreads across cache sets instead of colliding. Direct-mapped and set-associative caches thrash when hot addresses alias; coloring assigns pages to spread them. OS page allocators implement it.

demo.title: Demo — Cache Coloring

title: Lock-Free MPSC Queues
description: Builds multi-producer single-consumer queues with cache-line-separated head and tail. Producers contend on the tail line, the consumer owns the head line, and they never share. It is the workhorse of message passing.
key_mechanisms: Separate head and tail cache lines
Use atomic CAS on the tail

demo.title: Demo — Lock-Free MPSC Queues

title: Per-CPU Data Structures
description: Keeps per-CPU copies of hot data so cores never share cache lines. Updates touch only the local copy; aggregation reads all copies rarely. The kernel uses this pattern everywhere.

demo.title: Demo — Per-CPU Data Structures

title: Hot/Cold Field Splitting
description: Splits frequently-accessed fields from rarely-touched ones into separate structs. Hot fields pack into few cache lines; cold fields stop polluting the cache. It is mechanical and reliably effective.
key_mechanisms: Link with a pointer or index

demo.title: Demo — Hot/Cold Field Splitting

title: Huge Page Mapping
description: Backs large hot data with huge pages to cut TLB misses. Fewer, larger pages mean the TLB covers more memory; workloads with big footprints see clear wins. Transparent huge pages automate it.
key_mechanisms: Map hot regions with huge pages

demo.title: Demo — Huge Page Mapping

title: Write-Combining Stores
description: Uses non-temporal stores for streaming writes that will not be reread. Bypassing the cache avoids polluting it with write-once data; memcpy implementations use them for large copies. It keeps the cache for data that matters.

demo.title: Demo — Write-Combining Stores

title: Cache-Oblivious Algorithms
description: Designs algorithms that are cache-efficient at every level without tuning for specific sizes. Recursive divide-and-conquer keeps working sets small naturally; matrix transpose and sorting have cache-oblivious forms. They perform well on unknown hardware.

demo.title: Demo — Cache-Oblivious Algorithms

title: Perf Counter Validation
description: Validates layout changes with hardware performance counters, not just wall time. LLC misses, TLB misses, and coherence traffic prove the mechanism worked. Counters turn cache tuning from art to measurement.

demo.title: Demo — Perf Counter Validation

title: Struct Packing Discipline
description: Orders struct fields by decreasing size to minimize padding waste. Compilers insert padding for alignment; sorting fields largest-first packs them tightly. Smaller structs mean more fit in each cache line.

demo.title: Demo — Struct Packing Discipline

title: Read-Mostly Replication
description: Replicates read-mostly data per core with RCU-style updates. Readers never lock or share lines; writers publish new versions and wait for grace periods. It scales reads perfectly.
key_mechanisms: Replicate per core or per node

demo.title: Demo — Read-Mostly Replication

title: Interleave Policy Tuning
description: Tunes NUMA interleave policies for bandwidth-bound shared data. Striping pages across nodes aggregates their memory bandwidth; local placement would bottleneck one node. HPC codes interleave deliberately.

demo.title: Demo — Interleave Policy Tuning
